CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
January 11, 2023 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

Until further notice, meetings of the Inglewood Planning Commission will
be conducted pursuant to California Government Code section 54953(e),
which allows the City to use teleconferencing for members of the public
to access a meeting and to address the legislative body via a call-in
option.

CALL-IN OPTION
1. Members of the public who wish to attend the Planning Commission
Meeting of January 11, 2023 and address the Planning Commission must use
the call-in option noted below:

Instructions: Dial one of the  Phone  Numbers  below  and  when
prompted, enter the Access Code:

  Phone Number: 888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 9645704#

In the event of a disruption which prevents the City from broadcasting
the meeting to the public using the call-in option, or in the event of
a disruption within the City’s control which prevents the public from
offering public comments using the call-in option, the Planning
Commission shall take no further action on items appearing on the meeting
agenda until public access to the meeting via the call-in option is
restored.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City also provides alternative methods for members of the public to
submit comments and/or to observe a public meeting. The following
alternative methods are provided to the public as a matter of convenience
only and the disruption in service to any alternative method does not
preclude the Planning Commission from taking further action on an agenda
item.  In the event of a disruption to any alternative method below
members of the public should use the call-in option above.

2. Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public
may choose to submit comments for consideration by the Planning
Commission by sending them to Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of
the Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda, comments
must be received prior to 12:00 P.M. on the day of the meeting.
Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments
received after 12:00 P.M. and prior to the close of the public hearing
will be made part of the official public record of the meeting.

3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please
  check with your cable provider for details
  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video at
  https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

Accessibility: If you will require special accommodations due to a
disability, please contact the Planning Division Office at (310) 412-
5230, One Manchester Boulevard, 4th Floor, Inglewood, California 90301.
All requests for accommodations must be received 48 hours prior to the
day of the hearing.

Español: "Si no entiende esta noticia o si necesita más información,
favor de llamar a este número (310) 412-5230."

[Agenda Items and Additional Public Access Options Listed on Following
Pages]
 1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to
  address the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda
  other than a public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  Minutes approval for December 7, 2022 Planning Commission
  meeting.

6.  PUBLIC HEARING:
  a. A public hearing to consider an application by Sandy Sigal
  for Special Use Permit No. 2022-009 (SP-2022-009) to allow
  a proposed beauty salon within 300 feet of a similar use
  on an approximately 0.69-acre lot in an existing shopping
  center on a C-2 (General Commercial)/ MU-1A (TOD Mixed
  Use 1A Overlay) zoned property at 2870 West Imperial
  Highway.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1)  Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2022-138; and
  2)  Adopt the attached resolution approving SP-2022-
  009 subject to 11 conditions, and/or add conditions
  as deemed appropriate.
  Item 6a Documents

7.  Commission Initiatives.

8.  Adjournment.

In the event that the Planning Commission meeting of January 11,
2023 is not held, or is concluded prior to a public hearing or
other agenda item being considered, the public hearing or non-
public hearing agenda item will automatically be continued to the
next regular Planning Commission meeting.

Hearing materials are available at:
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-
Commission-4 and at City Hall, 1st Floor Lobby Information Desk
during regular business hours. If any additional documents are
received for distribution to the Planning Commission after
publication of this Agenda but before 12:00 P.M. on the day of the
meeting, they will be made available for public inspection at the
following webpage:
https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/Planning-
Commission-4.

(Note: The above procedures are subject to change for future
Commission meetings. Please refer to future Planning Commission
agendas for public participation option procedures at that time.)

  NEXT REGULAR PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING:
  WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 1, 2023, 7:00 P.M.
  INGLEWOOD CITY HALL, COUNCIL CHAMBERS, NINTH FLOOR
  ONE WEST MANCHESTER BOULEVARD
  INGLEWOOD, CA 90301

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, JANUARY 11, 2023

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Special Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, January 11, 2023, in the Council
Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge
of Allegiance by Commissioner Patricia Patrick, the meeting was
called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aidé Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson, ECD Director
  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Christine Rivera, Assistant Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Wilcox, Planning Manager stated staff made revisions to Item
6A, copies were distributed to the Planning Commissioners and also
posted on the City’s website.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

(5) MINUTES:
Chairman Springs called for Minutes approval for the December 7,
2022 Planning Commission meeting.

MOTION:
Commissioner Rice made the motion to approve the December 7, 2022
Planning Commission Minutes and second by Commissioner Shaw-Williams.

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

(6) PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A. SPECIAL PERMIT USE NO. 2022-009 (SP-2022-009) 2870 WEST
IMPERIAL HIGHWAY: A public hearing to consider an application by
Sandy Sigal for Special Use Permit No. 2022-009 (SP-2022-009) to
allow a proposed beauty salon within 300 feet of a similar use on
an approximately 0.69-acre lot in an existing shopping center on
a C-2 (General Commercial)/ MU-1A (TOD Mixed Use 1A Overlay) zoned
property at 2870 West Imperial Highway.

Ms. Christine  Rivera,  Assistant  Planner,  made  the  staff
presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
January 11, 2023

Commissioner Rice asked staff for clarification regarding the use
of the similar use.
 as Asked about the services provided at the similar use nearby,
  Nail Salon Spa?
  - Ms. Rivera responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff-
 Asked if there would be a difference in services as compared
  to the nearby similar use?
  - Ms. Rivera responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about their project.

Mr. John Brooks, representing the applicant.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick made a comment to the applicant –
 The nearby use specializes in Nails, Pedicures and Eyebrows.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant –
 Will Phenix suites be licensed by the State of California as
  a Salon itself?
  - Mr. Brooks responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.
 The Laws in California requires that someone would have to
  establish the license, and if Phenix does not establish the
  license, then will Phenix rent out booth space and that all of
  the cosmetologist who rent will just have to acquire a tax
  certificate?
 Is Phenix’s Business Model requiring all hair stylist to have
  either a Business License or a Trade license?
   Mr. Brooks responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.
 So you’re saying that Phenix Suites is a large capacity
  landlord who will host up to 82 independent business licensed
  hair salons in the building.
   Mr. Brooks responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
 If there are Phenix Salons located in Southern California area,
  and if this is the first, why did you decide to select the
  City of Inglewood?
  - Mr. Brooks responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated that she was familiar with the
Phenix type salons.

Chairman Springs stated to the applicant –
 This establishment is set as “by appointment only”, no “walk-
  ins”?
  - Mr. Brooks responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
 With regards to the rental of the booths, how is it handled and
  are they rented daily, weekly, monthly or annually?
   Mr. Brooks responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
 Who is Sandy Sigal with regard to this project and is he on the
  line right now as the second caller?
   Ms. Rivera responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
   Mr. Darren Bovard, Sr. Vice President, Representative for the
  New Mark Merrill Co., who are the present landlords for the
  plaza.
  2
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
January 11, 2023

Commissioner Trejo made a statement to both the applicant and the
representative –
 That it is imperative that the applicant come before the
  planning commission ready to answer all questions and should
  they not be in attendance and only for the reason of foreign
  travel or health issues, and there is a replacement attending
  the meeting, that replacement must have all the answers as would
  the applicant, otherwise the item is subject to be continued.

Ms. Wilcox made a suggestion to Chairman Springs and the Planning
Commission regarding the condition in the Resolution requiring
that Salons be licensed by the State, but to add that all
Individual Stylists also appropriately be licensed by the State.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
further questions for the applicant, there were none, and called
for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Rice motioned to affirm categorical exemption EA-CE-
2022-138 and adopt the attached resolution approving SP-2022-009
subject to the 11 conditions, plus two more conditions adding
Business License Requirements in the condition and was seconded by
Commissioner Shaw-Williams Resolution No. 1946

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A
  SPECIAL  USE  PERMIT  TO  SANDY  SIGAL,
  REPRESENTING NEWMARK MERRILL COMPANIES FOR
  UPSIDE CRENSHAW HOLDINGS, LLC TO ALLOW A
  BEAUTY SALON, WITHIN 300 FEET OF A SIMILAR USE
  ON AN APPROXIMATELY 0.69 ACRE, C-2 (GENERAL
  COMMERCIAL)/MU-1A (TOD MIXED USE 1A OVERLY)
  ZONED PROPERTY AT 2870 WEST IMPERIAL HIGHWAY.

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs.

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

(7) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None, (Confirmed by the AT&T Operator).

(8) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:
Commissioner Patrick –
 Question to staff regarding no designated stopping areas for
  Uber and Lyft vehicles for passenger unloading and loading, if
  so then where?
   Mr. Jackson responded to Commissioner Patrick’s statement.

Commissioner Rice -
 There will be a postponement of the Martin Luther King, Jr.,
  Festival on Market Street to February 18, 2023. Everyone is
  invited.

  3
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
January 11, 2023

Commissioner Trejo –
 Wanting to piggy-back on Commissioner Patrick’s question
  regarding the Uber and Lyft drivers who do not take their
  passengers to the So-Fi Stadium drop-off point, what is the
  repercussion of that action on the drivers?
   Mr. Jackson responded to Commissioner Trejo’s statement.
 Question to staff regarding the 405 Fwy, and the underpass
  filled with the homeless still and all of the trash and debris
  on the highway, is there something that can be done about this,
  it gives a bad look for the City of Inglewood with these new
  stadiums, the Forum and soon the new Shopping Plaza?
   Mr. Jackson responded to Commissioner Trejo’s statement.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams -
 Happy New Year to all and Happy Birthday to both Chairman
  Springs and Commissioner Rice.

Chairman Springs –
 Projects located at the corners of La Brea and Florence – what
  will the names of those complexes be called?
   Ms. Wilcox responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
   Mr. Jackson also responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
 The hotel at Hollywood Park Tomorrow, when is the completion
  date for that?
   Ms. Wilcox responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
 What will be the timeframe for the New Apartments there, start
  and completion dates?
   Mr. Jackson responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
 Statement to Mr. Ikemefuna – Next Year!

Commissioner Trejo –
 When is the next So-Fi Big Event?
   Mr. Jackson responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

(9) ADJOURNMENT:
Chairman Springs gave closing comments and wished Happy Birthday
to all, and Meeting adjourned at 7:52p.m.
